title: Find a pair matching a target in a sorted array
storyTitle: Two books for one gift voucher
summary: Find two different books on a price-sorted shelf whose prices add up exactly to a gift voucher.
goal: Choose two different books whose prices add up to the voucher

mapping.formal: Output [i, j], or null if none

examples.label: No pair works
examples.explanation: No two different books total 7, so the answer is null.

examples.label: Two equal prices
examples.explanation: Two different books can share a price: 3 + 3 = 6 at positions 0 and 1.

ladder.name: Check every pair
ladder.idea: Fix one book, then try it with every book after it. Move to the next book and repeat until a pair totals the voucher.

ladder.name: Search for the partner
ladder.idea: Each book needs a partner costing exactly `target − price`. The shelf is sorted, so binary-search the books to its right for that price.
ladder.insight: Once one book is chosen, the partner's price is known exactly. A sorted shelf lets us find a known price in log n steps instead of scanning.

ladder.name: Opposite pointers
ladder.idea: Start at the cheapest and the most expensive book. Too small: drop the cheapest. Too large: drop the most expensive. Each comparison rules out one book for good.
ladder.insight: Comparing the two ends tells us which end can never be part of an answer, so we can drop a whole book per step instead of searching for each partner.

approaches.name: Check every pair
approaches.summary: Fix one book, then try it with every book after it.

approaches.name: Opposite pointers
approaches.summary: Start at the cheapest and the most expensive book and rule out one end per comparison.

transfer.problem: Song lengths are listed from shortest to longest. Find two different songs that fill a 30-minute drive exactly.
transfer.explanation: The list is sorted and you need a pair with an exact total. Start at both ends: too short rules out the shortest song, too long rules out the longest.

selfCheck: Returns positions, not prices, and counts them from 0.
Never uses the same book twice, even when one price is exactly half the voucher.
Returns null (None) when no pair works, including for an empty shelf or a single book.
Every pass of the loop moves exactly one pointer inward, so the loop always ends.
